name: Undifferentiated content priority
summary: A composition that assigns effectively equal prominence to genuinely unequal content roles risks making it harder to locate the primary topic or next step.
recurring_structure: Main content, headings, supporting metadata, local navigation and minor details receive little differentiating typography, grouping, proximity or layout prominence despite distinct task priority.
harm_mechanism: Without adequate structural cues, finding key topics or following topic/subtopic relationships may require extra effort; WAI and design-system guidance describe navigational benefits of structured headings/regions and content hierarchy.
context: Pages with distinct main tasks and supporting content; visual and semantic relationships actually differ.
applicability: Observed unmarked hierarchy in content with genuinely unequal user-task priorities.
legitimate_contexts: Intentionally balanced items of genuinely equal priority.
Dense tabular or catalog presentation where uniformity improves comparison.
Minimalist layout whose heading/landmark semantics still distinguish information.

usability: Potential loss of scannability; inferential, not measured in W03.
accessibility: May mask programmatic relationships if semantic headings/landmarks also absent; appearance alone cannot prove WCAG failure.
maintainability: No verified maintenance harm from equal visual weight alone.

counterexamples.summary: A catalog grid may intentionally make similarly important entries visually equal.
counterexamples.context: Scanning comparable alternatives instead of following a single primary task.

version_context: WAI and official system reference docs unpinned; WCAG 2.2 (2024)
